summary: An aspiring artist in Texas was contacted by a scammer who used AI-generated video and voice to pose as a famous rapper, offered to promote her music, then asked for money. She recognised the scam and did not pay.
technical_summary: A scammer used AI voice and face mimicry on a live call to impersonate a celebrity, then moved the target to an upload portal and requested payment for radio play. The scheme mirrored a scam the celebrity had publicly warned about.

summary: After the 2023 Turkey-Syria earthquakes, scammers posted emotive images, some not real, with links to cryptocurrency wallets and fake donation appeals on TikTok and Twitter, diverting donations from real relief efforts.
technical_summary: Scammers used fabricated or recycled disaster imagery, including at least one reportedly AI-created picture, in social posts and live streams to solicit donations to personal wallets and accounts. Platform moderation did not prevent the campaign quickly.

summary: A coalition of rights groups challenged in court a French welfare agency algorithm that scores recipients' likelihood of overpayment, alleging it discriminates against disabled people and single mothers and invades privacy.
technical_summary: A risk-scoring model assigns every household member a score from 0 to 1 using personal data and flags high scorers for intrusive investigation. Criteria such as low income and disability-related work raise scores. The source code is not public, and the system has operated since the 2010s.

technical_summary: The suit says GPT-4o gave inaccurate reassurance and home-management advice over months, used a sycophantic tone and the user's faith, and its safety features did not reliably redirect him to professional care. Allegations are unproven.

summary: A Broadway performer and radio host reportedly lost access to his Facebook page after a scammer posing as a comedian's podcast team sent a personalised invitation, likely written with AI, and guided him through account permissions.
technical_summary: Fraudsters used highly personalised, probably LLM-composed invitations from impersonated podcast hosts to lure guests into handing over money, credentials or control of social accounts. The reported case involved a fake technical setup that transferred page access.

summary: Scammers in Australia used AI-generated deepfake videos of doctors and TV hosts to promote a diabetes supplement and give false medical claims. A diabetes expert said patients called his clinic about the fake ad.
technical_summary: Generative AI created realistic video and altered speech of real health experts and a TV presenter to deliver false endorsements and claims, such as that a common diabetes drug is inadequate or dangerous. The ads ran on Facebook and linked to fabricated interviews.

summary: Hong Kong police arrested 31 people in a syndicate that used AI-generated images of attractive women to run romance and investment scams on victims in Taiwan, Singapore and Malaysia. About HK$34 million in proceeds was intercepted.
technical_summary: Syndicate members used deepfake images to pose as wealthy single women, following scripted conversation guides to build trust and steer victims towards fraudulent crypto investments.

summary: After a fatal school-minibus crash in South Africa, AI-generated memorial posters showing invented child portraits circulated on social media before official victim details were released. AFP confirmed the images were AI-made, and officials criticised the posts.
technical_summary: AI image tools were used to create fabricated faces and memorial graphics purporting to show the crash victims. The faces did not match official photos, and the posters spread thousands of times across Facebook, X and TikTok.

sector.quote: The posters were shared thousands of times on Facebook, X and TikTok.

harm_type.quote: the posters announcing planned memorials for the children who died were fabricated

notes: The motive of the posters' creators is not stated.

summary: Researchers found 212 underground services built on large language models for cybercrime, such as WormGPT and FraudGPT, many using jailbroken mainstream models to write malware, phishing emails and scam sites.
technical_summary: Criminals either jailbreak commercial LLMs to bypass safeguards or use uncensored models behind services marketed on dark web markets and messaging apps. These tools automate phishing, malware generation and scam content creation.

summary: McDonald's piloted an AI voice ordering system, developed with IBM, at US drive-thrus and customers posted videos of frequent errors, such as adding unwanted items or picking up neighbouring-lane orders. McDonald's ended the IBM pilot in 2024.
technical_summary: A voice-recognition ordering bot misheard or mixed speech, including crosstalk from adjacent lanes, and ignored corrections, producing wrong orders. Reported accuracy was in the low 80% range, below the company's 95%-plus target.

summary: A user created a chatbot on Character.AI imitating a young woman murdered in 2006, without her family's consent. About 70 people chatted with it before the company removed it, admitting a policy violation, after her relatives objected publicly.
technical_summary: Character.AI lets users create public chatbot characters from any real or fictional source. A user built an avatar of a real murder victim and published it. The platform's impersonation policy was enforced only after the family raised it on social media.
